headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: Windsurf can write/modify shared workspace state while Whisper is read-only, but prompt-injection and leakage are limited by Whisper’s lack of interactive outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Whisper has no interactive tool use, filesystem write, or network egress, so it cannot be a meaningful injection source. Windsurf can read workspace files and use MCP/clipboard, so if Whisper outputs are manually copied into Windsurf, malicious text could be interpreted as instructions. The bridge is manual and limited.
conditions: IF Whisper outputs are manually pasted into Windsurf prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF Windsurf is configured to ingest workspace text as instructions, copied Whisper output can steer actions.
mitigations: Avoid copy-pasting raw Whisper transcripts into Windsurf prompts.
Wrap Whisper output in quoted/plain-text blocks.
Use a separate review step before any Windsurf action.
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf for untrusted text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between transcription and agent prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Whisper touches audio/speech and has no filesystem read, write, or network egress, while Windsurf reads workspace files and can send context to model proxies/MCP servers. The pair can leak data only if audio transcripts are placed into shared workspace or pasted into Windsurf; the default profiles do not show automatic sharing.
conditions: IF audio transcripts are saved into the shared workspace, Windsurf can read them.
IF Windsurf sends workspace context to its model proxy or MCP server, transcript contents may leave the local machine.
mitigations: Keep transcripts outside the shared workspace.
Redact sensitive audio before transcription review.
Restrict Windsurf to a dedicated non-sensitive folder.
Turn off unnecessary MCP servers.
requires-engineering: enforce per-folder access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Whisper cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. Windsurf can write files and modify git state, but the other agent lacks overlapping write capabilities. The only plausible conflict is indirect via shared files, which is limited and not a true concurrent write race.
conditions: IF Whisper is wrapped by an external script that writes files, overlap could emerge.
IF Windsurf instances share the same workspace and auto-save concurrently, file contention can occur.
mitigations: Keep Whisper as read-only CLI usage.
Use separate workspaces per Windsurf session.
Disable auto-save during critical edits.
Avoid running multiple Windsurf instances on the same repo.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared outputs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Whisper can produce transcripts that Windsurf may treat as source material, and Windsurf has tool-use and file-edit authority. If Windsurf accepts transcription output without verification, transcription errors can cascade into code changes or commands. Whisper is not authoritative by itself, but Windsurf’s default agentic loop makes this a realistic downstream risk.
conditions: IF Whisper transcripts are used as authoritative requirements, Windsurf may act on transcription errors.
IF Windsurf auto-executes commands, a bad transcription can trigger incorrect shell actions.
mitigations: Require human review of transcripts before action.
Compare transcripts against the original audio for critical tasks.
Disable Windsurf auto-execute.
Use checklists for code or command changes derived from transcripts.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before acting on transcription-derived text.

E_compliance.rationale: Whisper handles audio/speech, which may include regulated content, while Windsurf handles open files and can transmit context through model proxies and MCP servers. The profiles do not prove a specific residency or certification mismatch, so this is not high; however, the combination creates a plausible compliance gap if regulated audio is transcribed into a workspace that Windsurf uploads.
conditions: IF regulated audio is transcribed into files that Windsurf processes, compliance obligations may attach.
IF Windsurf sends those files to external model services without a DPA, residency or retention issues can arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated audio out of Windsurf workspaces.
Use a documented DPA and retention policy for any uploaded content.
Limit MCP servers to approved endpoints.
Review provider data-processing terms before use.
requires-engineering: segregate regulated workloads into a compliant environment.
